claims: Cancer is a group of over 100 diseases.
Cancer is characterized by uncontrolled cell growth.
Uncontrolled cell growth in cancer can invade nearby tissues.
Uncontrolled cell growth in cancer can spread to other parts of the body.
Metastasis is the spread of cancer to other parts of the body.
Cancer is caused by genetic mutations from environmental factors, lifestyle, or inheritance.
Cancer is diagnosed via scans, labs, and biopsies.
CT scans help identify tumor locations and sizes.
MRIs help identify tumor locations and sizes.
X-rays help identify tumor locations and sizes.
PET scans help identify tumor locations and sizes.
A biopsy involves removing a tissue sample and examining it under a microscope.
Blood tests can detect abnormal cell counts or specific tumor markers.
Urine tests can detect abnormal cell counts or specific tumor markers.
Physical exam and history provide initial detection based on symptoms and checking for abnormal lumps.
Surgery aims to remove the tumor.
Chemotherapy uses drugs to kill rapidly dividing cancer cells throughout the body.
Radiation therapy uses high-energy radiation to target and kill cancer cells.
Targeted therapy targets specific genetic changes in cancer cells.
Immunotherapy boosts the immune system to fight the cancer.
Targeted therapy and immunotherapy are newer treatments.
Metastasis is when cancer spreads to distant parts of the body.
The World Health Organization (WHO) highlights that tobacco use, unhealthy diet, alcohol consumption, and physical inactivity are major risks.
